observation.visible_scene: A single transparent marquise/oval-cut faceted gemstone rests on a glossy black reflective surface against a pure black background. A mirror-image reflection of the stone appears directly below it on the surface. The gemstone's outline, position on the frame, and orientation stay essentially fixed throughout the excerpt; the reflection likewise stays locked beneath it.
visible_changes: The internal facet pattern continuously changes: bright white facets and dark facets shift in position and intensity across the stone, and colored dispersion flashes (blue, yellow, orange, green, red) appear and fade on different facets.
A bright starburst/lens-flare emerges near the lower-right edge of the stone (around the middle of the segment), grows, then subsides; the reflection shows a corresponding bright patch.
Near the end, a green-then-orange/yellow flare appears at the left tip of the stone, while the earlier lower-right flare has faded.
The reflection below tracks these luminance changes, brightening and dimming in sync with the stone above.
No translation of the stone across the frame and no obvious change in its silhouette/tilt is visible; the apparent motion is the play of light, not object displacement.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the changing sparkle is caused by the gem rotating on a turntable, a moving/rotating light source, or camera motion is not determinable from this segment.
What happens before the first frame and after the last frame (e.g., continued rotation or flare sequence) is unknown.
uncertain_details: Slight in-plane orientation differences between frames could indicate a very slow rotation about a vertical axis, but the outline is too stable to confirm; the dominant visible effect is scintillation rather than geometric motion.
Background dust specks are too sparse to confirm any camera drift, so camera movement is uncertain.
The flare/starburst shapes are lens/optical artifacts of the bright facets, not separate physical objects.
